title: Ṣarf and naḥw in the Ottoman madrasa
summary: The Ottoman madrasa reads five books of ṣarf, from al-Amthila to Marāḥ al-arwāḥ, then Birgivī's two books of naḥw and al-Kāfiya with Molla Câmî.

sections.heading: Five books of ṣarf
paragraphs: The Ottoman student began with al-Amthila (Emsile), the conjugation tables of نَصَرَ, then Bināʾ al-afʿāl, al-Maqṣūd, al-Taṣrīf al-ʿIzzī and Marāḥ al-arwāḥ. The five are still printed together as one collection of ṣarf.
Al-Maqṣūd is attributed to Abū Ḥanīfa; the attribution is doubted, but the book kept its place in the Ḥanafī madrasa.

sections.heading: Birgivī and the Kāfiya
paragraphs: Naḥw begins with Imām Birgivī's al-ʿAwāmil, which arranges grammar as sixty governors, thirty governed words and ten states, then his Iẓhār al-asrār. The student then reads Ibn al-Ḥājib's al-Kāfiya with Jāmī's commentary, known in Turkish as Molla Câmî.
These books are still taught in Turkey and the Balkans, and The Nahwi's Ottoman path follows them in this order.
